challenge.better_approach: Make _durability_roots skip a repo outside a scratch HOME. Considered: that bends the judge for a proof's sake and would hide a real crossing's commons when a judge runs under a scratch HOME on purpose; the proof's world is the proof's to build, and the sibling helper _cross_to_proved already builds it right. Fixing the tooth is the smaller change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the launched CodeMother's ticket_file._TICKETS is bent by CAIRN_BUILD_INSPECTOR_TICKET_STORE under a scratch HOME (inspector.py:2568, _root_override refuses it under the live HOME): the tester runs proofs under a scratch HOME, so it holds; measured on the stones harness.
challenge.prior_art: Grepped tickets and questions for the_stones_are_pushed and 973574dddb77. 973574dddb77 (D1/D2) moved this tooth's boat into the fixture registry, but patched _tfile._TICKETS in the proof's own process only. 3e08102ef35a gave inspect_wire.launch its ticket_store root (used by _cross_to_proved, not by this tooth). 03daad62ef1b (TICKETME) would REPORT a proof patching a name a judge reads in another process; this tooth is one such case. None fixes this tooth.
challenge.real_collision: None. 973574dddb77's intent (the tooth never reads the live commons) is what this restores; this is its residue across the process boundary.

answers.falsifier: with the sibling commons one commit ahead of its upstream, test_clearance stays green; inside the tooth's world the durability root for its ticket lies under the fixture registry, not the commons beside the code.
answers.from_idea: none, because the finding was measured on the off-main stones harness (akiendelllinux /var/tmp/stones.oqXCpW/B, cairn at 3c6c6c3a1 with its sibling CairnCommons one commit ahead) and directed straight to a cast by the orchestrator, not captured first
answers.how: Wrap the tooth's clear() in inspect_wire.launch(berths=<tmp>/no-chart-berths, ticket_store=_FIXTURE_TICKETS), exactly as _cross_to_proved does at test_clearance.py:1727; add teeth that ask the_stones_are_pushed inside the same world and assert its roots lie under the fixture world.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (a hollow green is worse than a red: a tooth whose verdict is the operator's push state is leaned on as a clearance verdict) and RULE 1 (the judge runs in another process; the proof's in-process patch does not reach it, so the root must ride the launch).
answers.what: test_clearance's gated-crossing tooth crosses PROVED inside a CodeMother launched over its fixture registry, so its verdict never depends on the push state of the commons beside the code.

bullets.text: The escaped branch: _durability_roots' tk-found branch. The judge's own find_ticket globbed '*-an-intention-declares-its-gated-hands.json' in the commons beside the code (0354c0269ff7-...json), so tk.parent was that commons; the proof's patch of _tfile._TICKETS lived only in the proof's process.
The tooth's own check at test_clearance.py:1008 (_t._find_ticket in the patched proof process) is blind to the judge's process, which is why it stayed green while the judge read the live commons.
